summary: Lotte Korea PP yarn/inj offered ~1,300; buyers bid 1,250-1,260 USD/ton CIF
Imported PP set new high 1,300+ USD/ton CIF as China offers prompt cargoes
Domestic NSRP/BSR/Hyosung yarn tested up to VND 40,000/kg
paras: Yesterday, South Korea's Lotte Chemical issued new offers for PP and PE products to the Vietnamese market: PP yarn/injection grades were offered at USD 1,310/tonne/CIF, PP Film/transparent/fibre at USD 1,350-1,380; PP random at USD 1,400-1,410/tonne/CIF, and PP Lami and coating at USD 1,450/tonne/CIF… for October 2026 delivery.

Some domestic buyers said they had successfully bid for Lotte's imported PP homo (yarn/injection) at USD 1,250-1,260/tonne/CIF that same afternoon. However, by this morning, September 11, the distributor had temporarily halted sales at the above bid level; then, in the early afternoon, it raised the PP yarn offer to USD 1,330/tonne/CIF, up USD 20/tonne from yesterday's offer. Lotte's settled sale price for M9600 PP coating was reported at USD 1,430/tonne/CIF, just USD 20/tonne below yesterday's offer list, with no volume discounts.

Imported PP set a new high of USD 1,300/tonne/CIF and above, as most Chinese producers also offered prompt-delivery cargoes at this level (offers for October delivery were lower, around USD 1,260-1,270/tonne/CIF). Meanwhile, Thailand's IRPC offered its 1102K and K1111 PP yarn/injection grades at USD 1,400/tonne/CFR HCMC, PP 1100RC at USD 1,450/tonne/CFR, and PP Film 1126NK at USD 1,490/tonne/CIF…

Domestically, some traders today tested new offer levels by raising offers for NSRP-, BSR- and Hyosung Vina-origin PP yarn/injection to VND 40,000/kg including VAT — level with the “peak” set this past March-April. Even so, sources said these offers are mainly intended to gauge market response and to shape a high price base for early next week, with no transactions recorded yet. Some other sellers kept their offers in the VND 39,200-39,500/kg including VAT range, likewise closing few deals.

In line with the general trend for homopolymer grades, offers for other PP products also rose. For PP random, for example, the Hyosung Vina plant offered R701N at VND 37,800/kg excluding VAT (about VND 40,800/kg including 8% VAT), while on the market many traders offered up to VND 42,000/kg including VAT. PP Film/coating (white) grades of Thai and Korean origin… were likewise offered higher at around VND 42,000/kg including VAT; while PP copolymer offers were commonly reported in the VND 39,500-41,000/kg including VAT range…

Prompt September-delivery cargoes were offered high, but for October delivery some sellers offered noticeably lower. For example, one distributor today offered S-Oil (South Korea)-origin HD500 PP yarn at VND 37,700/kg including VAT and delivery, for October delivery…

The volume of imported offers was greater rather than short this week, but import offer prices had risen too high, so most buyers were reluctant to commit to imports. Customers chose to turn back to the domestic market, seeking cargoes available from local inventories. This has further accelerated the drawdown of PP stocks held by domestic traders, helping to push prices up. Some sources said operating rates at several PP producers in Vietnam remain above 100%.

Across the wider region, according to Platts assessments, in Northeast Asia the general price level for PP yarn/injection rose USD 30/tonne this week, PP Film rose USD 45/tonne, BOPP rose USD 45/tonne, and PP block copolymer rose USD 35/tonne from the previous week. In Southeast Asia, prices for all PP grades surged USD 95/tonne this week, with PP yarn/injection up to USD 1,250/tonne/CFR, BOPP to USD 1,270/tonne/CFR, and IPP Film and block copolymer to USD 1,300/tonne/CFR.

PP prices in Asia rose sharply this week, driven by gains in crude oil futures, which in turn lifted the price of the propylene feedstock. In China, demand climbed as producers planned to raise operating rates to build stocks ahead of the Golden Week holiday in early October. Domestic inventories in China were low, as many plants had cut operating rates due to excessively high feedstock costs.

summary: Premium LLDPE (Qamar FD21HS, Sabic 218WJ) offered up to VND 40,000/kg
China oil-based LLDPE Film 1,310-1,320; OQ Oman 1,300 USD/ton CIF
NE Asia HDPE fell 10 USD (Platts); buyers wary at feedstock-driven highs
paras: Yesterday, the distributor of South Korea's Lotte Chemical issued new offers for PP and PE products to the Vietnamese market. As of today, September 11, some domestic buyers had successfully closed imports of Lotte's HDPE yarn at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF; while LLDPE Film and injection grades were both settled at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF, just USD 10/tonne below the offer price.

For Middle Eastern material, one distributor offered LLDPE Film F1801SA (MI 1) of OQ Oman origin to the Vietnamese market at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF Hai Phong, with a latest shipment date (LSD) of October 20, 2026. The distributor noted that volumes were small, only about 6 containers. Another distributor quoted a bid-taking price for Saudi Arabia's Sabic HDPE Film bimodal 0851P — re-exported from China to Vietnam — at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF, for September delivery, with a volume of about 6 containers.

For Chinese material, oil-based LLDPE Film was commonly offered at USD 1,310-1,320/tonne/CIF Vietnam. For example, one distributor offered Petrochina-origin LLDPE Film 2020F (oil-based) to Vietnam at USD 1,310/tonne/CIF. Meanwhile, coal-based LLDPE Film was offered lower, commonly at USD 1,245-1,275/tonne/CIF.

For Southeast Asian material, after Lotte Korea announced its new offers, many buyers continued to inquire about additional Thai PE, but PTT's distributor had suspended sales (earlier this week it sold LLDPE injection at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF and settled HDPE yarn/film at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF), possibly to hold stock and push prices higher in the coming days. PTT also did not offer LDPE Film to Vietnam (it had offered at USD 1,500/tonne/CIF early in the week but subsequently closed no sales to customers), as it had already sold a fair amount of this material to other markets at USD 1,600/tonne/CIF and above.

For US material, PE offers to Vietnam were fairly plentiful, but prices were also rising. Today, the Itochu distributor in Thailand offered a range of PE products of US CIPLAS origin, with LDPE offers up USD 30-40/tonne from the previous week to USD 1,400-1,420/tonne/CIF depending on grade; LLDPE Film grades offered at USD 1,170/tonne/CIF, up USD 10/tonne; and HDPE blow grades from CIPLAS and Ineos at USD 1,170-1,230/tonne/CIF depending on grade, up USD 30/tonne from the previous week, with delivery expected in mid-October…

Domestically, spot offer prices for LLDPE rose steadily this week, with “premium” grades such as Qamar's FD21HS and Sabic's 218WJ now offered as high as VND 41,500-42,000/kg including VAT (up about VND 2,500-3,000/kg from the start of the week), prompting many buyers to stay on the sidelines and watch further. Chinese-origin LLDPE Film was also offered up to VND 38,500-39,500/kg including VAT, depending on grade and supplier.

However, for LLDPE film with far-forward October delivery, offer levels were notably lower, commonly at VND 37,500-39,000/kg including VAT depending on origin. Even Sabic's LLDPE 218WJ grade saw some sellers offering at VND 38,600/kg including VAT for mid-October delivery.

Similarly, spot LDPE was also offered at very high levels, around VND 43,000-45,000/kg including VAT. For example, one distributor offered Borouge (UAE)-origin LDPE Film FT6236 at VND 44,300/kg including VAT, a sharp rise of up to VND 4,000/kg from the transaction price recorded at the start of the week.

For HDPE grades, offers were commonly at VND 39,000-43,000/kg including VAT. For Chinese material, for example, another distributor offered STL (China) HDPE FS7000 at VND 39,700/kg including VAT, Yulong's HDPE Film 7000F at VND 38,700/kg including VAT, Yulong's HDPE Film TR571 at VND 39,600/kg including VAT, and Yulong's HDPE blow 5502S at VND 38,300/kg including VAT… For Middle Eastern material, HDPE Film products were commonly offered at VND 42,000-43,000/kg including VAT…

“The PE price level is currently at a resistance threshold. Processing buyers dare not buy additional volumes because, at current feedstock prices, finished goods would run at a loss since end-product prices have not risen correspondingly. Conversely, on the sellers' side, PE offers are unlikely to cool immediately while crude oil prices keep rising. The PE market early next week may see a tug-of-war, and resin prices could ease if oil prices fall,” a source analyzed.

Across the wider region, according to Platts assessments, in Northeast Asia the general price level for HDPE Film/yarn/blow/injection fell USD 10/tonne from the previous week, LDPE fell USD 15/tonne, while LLDPE rose USD 10/tonne. Conversely, in Southeast Asia, prices for all HDPE grades rose strongly by USD 30/tonne this week to USD 1,240-1,250/tonne/CFR, LLDPE fell USD 10/tonne to USD 1,190/tonne/CFR, metallocene C6 LDPE fell USD 10/tonne to USD 1,340/tonne/CFR, and LDPE held flat from the previous week at USD 1,600/tonne/CFR.

Asia's PE market moved in mixed directions this week, with prices still holding at high levels amid rising crude oil and ethylene costs. Cargoes from the Middle East and the US, though offered, were largely ignored by the market due to high prices and long delivery times. In Southeast Asia, supply remained tight owing to plant maintenance turnarounds under way in the region. However, a genuine demand-driven recovery has yet to materialize across Asia, as plastics converters and packaging producers continue to struggle with low order volumes from end-consumer markets.

summary: FPC raised Vietnam PVC offer 10 USD to 860-870 USD/ton CIF
Coal-based PVC scarcer as China coal feedstock costs jumped
China PVC +10 USD (Platts); oil-based FOB China 755 USD/ton
paras: FPC's distributor has announced adjustments to its PVC offer prices for cargoes delivering in late September 2026. Accordingly, the FOB Taiwan quotation rose USD 10/tonne to USD 820/tonne/FOB; FPC's PVC offers to China and Southeast Asia both rose USD 10/tonne, to USD 820 and USD 850/tonne/CIF respectively; while the offer to India continued to climb sharply, up USD 40/tonne to USD 950/tonne/CIF… These quotations do not include volume-based discounts.

Some sources said FPC's PVC offer price to Vietnam rose USD 10/tonne, in line with the general regional adjustment trend, to USD 860-870/tonne/CIF… Although the offer price increased, it carries little significance, because in practice Formosa's offered volumes are very small. Sources said Formosa has three cracking furnaces but currently only one is in operation. Formosa's PVC output has therefore fallen sharply due to the feedstock shortage, with volumes only sufficient for domestic consumption. Replenishing the remaining feedstock supply will take considerable time.

In a separate update today, distributor Itochu is offering TH1000 PVC from Japan's Taiyo, for October 2026 delivery to Vietnam, at USD 850-860/tonne/CIF, up USD 100/tonne from the previous month's price.

Meanwhile, offer prices for SE950/SE1000 PVC from the US producer Shintech to Vietnam this week were reported at USD 770-780/tonne/CIF, up a further USD 10-20/tonne from the previous week, with the cargo expected to arrive in January 2027.
Besides oil-based PVC, offers of coal-based PVC have also grown scarcer, as the price of the coal feedstock used to produce PVC in China has risen sharply — not to mention elevated freight rates…

As a result, PVC offer prices in Vietnam on today's end-of-week trading day were pushed up strongly, despite “sluggish” consumption. A source in the south said the general price level for oil-based PVC was driven up to VND 24,000-25,000/kg including VAT; coal-based PVC was likewise pushed up to VND 23,000-24,000/kg including VAT…
Similarly, in the north, most sellers have raised their offer prices for oil-based PVC products — covering both domestically sourced and imported material — to VND 24,300/kg including VAT and above…

Across the wider region, according to Platts assessments, the general PVC price level in China this week edged up USD 10/tonne from the previous week to USD 850/tonne/CFR; PVC prices in Southeast Asia rose more strongly, up USD 25/tonne from the previous week to USD 790/tonne/CFR.

Sources said the export price of ethylene-based (oil-based) PVC on an FOB China basis stood at USD 755/tonne this week; the export price of China's carbide-based (coal-based) PVC was USD 740/tonne/FOB, up as much as USD 20-25/tonne from the previous week.

PVC prices in Asia continued to rise this week, driven by higher input costs. Even so, export volumes remained limited, with high prices restraining buying demand. China's PVC export sales to Southeast Asia are said to be only moderate.
